mainTopic: Heaven's help toward holiness, and the יום כיפור lottery: how the lots were drawn, the lottery box, who draws, and the miracles of שמעון הצדיק's era.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משל from תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. A naphtha seller lets the buyer measure alone, but a balsam seller joins in. In the same way, Heaven only opens the door to sin but actively helps a person who does good. Next comes a teaching that sin dulls the heart, followed by two ברייתות: a little impurity leads to much impurity, and a little holiness leads to much holiness. Then the chapter אמר להם הממונה ends, and a new משנה describes the יום כיפור lottery. The כהן גדול mixes the lots in a קלפי, draws one in each hand, places them on the two goats, and declares 'לה׳ חטאת'. The גמרא explains that the mixing keeps the draw random. It also explains why the box was wooden, not holy, and only big enough for two hands. It then contrasts our משנה with רבי יהודה, who has the סגן draw too, and names רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים as the opposing view. Finally, a ברייתא lists the miracles of שמעון הצדיק's forty years and how they faded after him. It ends with a story about a greedy כהן whose nickname continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The parable of the naphtha seller and the balsam seller
steps.stepSummary: The parable continues: a merchant lets the naphtha buyer measure alone, but waits to measure balsam together with the buyer so both enjoy the scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone comes to measure naphtha, the seller tells him: 'Measure it yourself.' If someone comes to measure balsam, the seller tells him: 'Wait for me until I measure it with you, so that both you and I will smell nice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a parable from תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. The parable explains ריש לקיש's rule that a person heading toward sin is only given an opening, while a person heading toward purity gets active help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naphtha smells bad, so the seller does not want to get close. He lets the buyer serve himself. That is like Heaven merely 'opening the door' for someone who chooses sin. Balsam smells wonderful, so the seller eagerly joins in. That is like Heaven actively assisting someone who pursues מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: So that we will be perfumed / smell fragrant
Parable, a story used to illustrate an idea

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a parable. The opening of the parable, and ריש לקיש's statement it explains ('בא ליטמא פותחין לו, בא ליטהר מסייעין אותו'), come on the previous amud. The seller represents Heaven, and the buyer represents the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This parable is a basic source for the idea that a person who makes an effort toward good receives Heavenly help (סייעתא דשמיא). Sin, by contrast, is only permitted, not assisted.

phrases.english: If one comes to measure naphtha,
he says to him: Measure it yourself.
phrases.notes: The seller keeps his distance from the bad smell.

phrases.english: If one comes to measure balsam,
he says to him: Wait for me
until I measure it with you,
so that you and I will both be perfumed.
phrases.notes: The seller gladly joins in, like Heaven helping one who does good.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לִמְדּוֹד נֵפְטְ, אוֹמֵר לוֹ: מְדוֹד אַתָּה לְעַצְמְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the parable begun on the previous amud, which illustrates ריש לקיש's statement about Heaven's response to impurity versus purity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven merely allows the path to sin (like the naphtha seller), but actively joins and helps the path to good (like the balsam seller).

steps.title: Sin dulls a person's heart
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that sin stupefies the heart. He reads the word ונטמתם as if it said ונטמטם, meaning 'dulled.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: Sin dulls a person's heart. The פסוק says: 'Do not make yourselves impure with them, so that you become impure through them.' Do not read the word as 'and you become impure' (ונטמאתם). Read it as 'and you become dulled' (ונטמטם).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. It says sin does not only make a person impure, it also dulls his heart and mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק spells the word ונטמתם without an aleph, which is unusual. The ברייתא uses an אל תקרי reading to hear the root טמטום (dullness) in it. The message is that sin damages a person's spiritual sensitivity, which makes the next sin easier.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא source)
'Do not read': a method that rereads a word to draw out an extra lesson

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the actual text of the תורה. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
Sin stupefies the heart of a person,
as it is said: 'And do not impurify yourselves with them,
so that you become impure through them.'
phrases.notes: Spelled without an aleph, which hints at the reading that follows.

phrases.english: Do not read 'and you become impure,'
rather: 'and you become stupefied.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: עֲבֵירָה מְטַמְטֶמֶת לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching on the effect of sin: beyond Heaven merely allowing it, sin itself dulls the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sin causes טמטום הלב, a dulling of the heart, derived through an אל תקרי reading of ונטמתם.

steps.title: A little impurity leads to much impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who makes himself a little impure is made very impure, from below to above, and from this world to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Do not make yourselves impure with them, so that you become impure through them.' A person who makes himself impure a little is made impure a lot. If he does it below, he is made impure from above. If he does it in this world, he is made impure for עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same פסוק. It explains that the double language of impurity in the פסוק means impurity grows much bigger than the person's own act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the root טמא twice: once for what the person does, and once for what is done to him. The ברייתא reads this as a spiral in three ways: small becomes large, earthly becomes Heavenly, and this world carries into עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'They make him impure' (מטמאין אותו) refers to Heaven. It does not mean other people.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״(אַל) תִטַּמְּאוּ בָּהֶם וְנִטְמֵתֶם בָּם״,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'Do not impurify yourselves with them, so that you become impure through them':
a person who impurifies himself a little,
they impurify him greatly.
If below, they impurify him from above.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — מְטַמְּאִין אוֹתוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: If in this world, they impurify him for the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״(אַל) תִטַּמְּאוּ בָּהֶם וְנִטְמֵתֶם בָּם״, אָדָם מְטַמֵּא עַצְמוֹ מְעַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expounds the same פסוק from step 2 a second way, showing how impurity multiplies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small act of self-impurity leads to great impurity, imposed from Heaven and lasting into עולם הבא.

steps.title: A little holiness leads to much holiness
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ברייתא teaches that one who sanctifies himself a little is sanctified greatly, from above, and for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Sanctify yourselves, and you will be holy.' A person who makes himself holy a little is made holy a lot. If he does it below, he is made holy from above. If he does it in this world, he is made holy for עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the positive mirror image of the previous ברייתא. Holiness grows the same way impurity does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק (ויקרא יא:מד) also has a double language: 'sanctify yourselves' and 'you will be holy.' The ברייתא reads it with the same three-part spiral. This closes the circle with the balsam parable: a person's small effort toward good is met with much greater Heavenly help.
steps.whatToRemember: Both directions spiral upward. A small step into sin brings much more impurity, and a small step toward holiness brings much more holiness, both from Heaven and into עולם הבא. Heaven only opens the door to sin, but actively helps toward good.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a foundational source for the idea that a person only needs to begin. A small first effort at קדושה is met with great Heavenly help.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'Sanctify yourselves and you will be holy':
a person who sanctifies himself a little,
they sanctify him greatly.
If below, they sanctify him from above.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: If in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם וִהְיִיתֶם קְדוֹשִׁים״, אָדָם מְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ מְעַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The direct positive parallel to step 3, applying the same pattern to holiness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small act of self-sanctification leads to great holiness, granted from Heaven and lasting into עולם הבא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter אמר להם הממונה
steps.stepSummary: The previous chapter, אמר להם הממונה, formally ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'אמר להם הממונה'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter אמר להם הממונה. It is not part of the argument itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula expresses the learner's wish to return to and review the chapter just finished. It separates the previous chapter's discussion, which ended with the parables about טומאה and קדושה, from the new chapter about the lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula said at the end of a chapter
The appointed officer in the בית המקדש who ran the daily lotteries; the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you
'The appointed officer said to them'
phrases.notes: The name of the chapter being closed (the third chapter of יומא).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose final aggadic teachings appeared in steps 1-4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter אמר להם הממונה is complete; a new chapter begins.

steps.title: The new chapter opens: drawing the two lots
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול mixes the lots in a box and draws one in each hand. Whoever stands on the side of the 'לשם' lot announces it and tells him to raise that hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He mixed the lots in the box and brought up two lots. On one was written 'For ה׳' and on the other 'For עזאזל'. The סגן stood at his right and the ראש בית אב at his left. If the lot for ה׳ came up in his right hand, the סגן says to him: 'My master כהן גדול, raise your right hand.' If the lot for ה׳ came up in his left hand, the ראש בית אב says to him: 'My master כהן גדול, raise your left hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter's משנה begins by describing the lottery that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל. The official standing on the side where the 'לשם' lot came up tells the כהן גדול to raise that hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול pulls out both lots at once, one in each hand, so the result is random. Raising the hand shows everyone which side the 'לשם' lot is on. The person standing on that side, either the סגן or the ראש בית אב, gets the honor of announcing it.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery box or urn holding the lots
A lot: a marked token drawn to decide something by chance
The destination in the wilderness to which the שעיר המשתלח is sent on יום כיפור; the lot 'לעזאזל' marks that goat
The head of the family group of כהנים serving that day

steps.confusionAlert: Each hand holds one lot. 'Raise your right hand' does not mean only one lot was drawn. It means the 'לשם' lot is in that hand, so everyone can see it.

phrases.english: He mixed in the lottery box,
and brought up two lots,
one had written on it 'For ה׳',
and one had written on it 'For Azazel'.
The deputy was at his right,
and the head of the family group at his left.
If the lot for ה׳ came up in his right hand —
the deputy says to him:
My master, High Priest,
raise your right hand.
And if the lot for ה׳ came up in his left hand —
the head of the family group says to him:
My master, High Priest,
raise your left hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lots are mixed in a box and drawn together, one per hand. The official on the side of the 'לשם' lot announces it and has the כהן גדול raise that hand.

steps.title: Placing the lots on the goats and the declaration
steps.stepSummary: The lots are placed on the goats, and the כהן גדול says 'לה׳ חטאת'. רבי ישמעאל says 'לה׳' is enough. The people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He placed the lots on the two goats and said: 'For ה׳, a sin-offering.' רבי ישמעאל says: he did not need to say 'sin-offering', only 'For ה׳'. And they answer after him: 'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. The lots are placed on the goats, and the כהן גדול declares the goat for ה׳ a חטאת. רבי ישמעאל disagrees about the wording of that declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא requires the full declaration 'לה׳ חטאת'. רבי ישמעאל holds that saying just 'לה׳' is enough. When the people hear ה׳'s name, they respond with 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד'.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats (here, the two יום כיפור goats)
The תנא who holds that saying 'לה׳' alone is enough

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: The praise said in the מקדש in response to hearing ה׳'s name

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's procedure: mix, draw both lots, announce the 'לשם' hand, place the lots on the goats, declare 'לה׳ (חטאת)', and the people answer 'ברוך שם'.

phrases.english: He placed them on the two goats,
phrases.notes: The right-hand lot goes on the right goat and the left-hand lot on the left goat.

phrases.english: and says: 'For God, a sin-offering.'
Rabbi Yishmael says:
He did not need to say 'sin-offering',
but only 'For God'.
And they answer after him:
'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from drawing the lots to placing them on the goats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, the כהן גדול declares 'לה׳ חטאת'. According to רבי ישמעאל, 'לה׳' alone is enough. The people respond 'ברוך שם'.

steps.title: Why mix the lots in a box?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה requires the lots to be mixed in the box.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need 'he mixed in the box'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking the purpose of the first detail in the משנה, mixing the lots in the box. It sets up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lots could have been drawn without being mixed first. So the גמרא wants to know what problem the mixing solves.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
'Why do I need?': asks the purpose of a detail

phrases.english: Gemara:
Why do I need 'he mixed in the box'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the opening words of the משנה in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of mixing the lots in the box before drawing.

steps.title: So he cannot deliberately pick the lot
steps.stepSummary: Mixing makes sure the כהן גדול cannot intentionally grab the 'לשם' lot with his right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he will not aim and take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The mixing prevents the כהן גדול from deliberately choosing which lot ends up in which hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a good sign when the 'לשם' lot comes up in the right hand, so a כהן גדול might be tempted to steer the result. Mixing the lots in the box hides which lot is where. This keeps the drawing a true lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So that not': introduces a purpose or safeguard
He would intend or aim on purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the choice of the goats must truly be left to the lot. Anything that lets the כהן גדול control the outcome defeats the purpose of a גורל.

phrases.english: So that he will not intend
phrases.notes: That is, he will not aim for the 'לשם' lot with his right hand.

phrases.english: and take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mixing ensures randomness. It prevents the כהן גדול from intentionally taking the 'לשם' lot in his right hand.

steps.title: רבא describes the lottery box
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the קלפי was made of wood, was not holy (חול), and had room for only two hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The lottery box was made of wood. It was an ordinary, non-holy box. It was only big enough to fit two hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds details about the box the lots were mixed in. He tells us its material, its status, and its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before explained that mixing the lots stops the כהן גדול from picking on purpose. רבא's small size fits that goal, because there is no room to feel around for the right lot. The other two details, wood and not holy, will be questioned next.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or urn for drawing lots
Ordinary, not holy (not a sacred vessel)

phrases.english: Rava said:
The lottery box was made of wood,
and it was non-holy (ordinary),
and it held only two hands.
phrases.notes: It was too small to move the hands around and feel for a specific lot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds physical details about the box whose purpose was just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קלפי was wooden, non-holy, and held only two hands.

steps.title: רבינא asks why the box was not made holy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא accepts the small size. He challenges the 'non-holy' detail: why not make the box holy?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this. It makes sense that the box held only two hands, so the כהן גדול could not aim for a lot and take it. But why was it ordinary? Let it be made holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on one part of רבא's description. He says we should make the box a holy vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא' format means: one detail makes sense, but another does not. The size has a clear reason. The non-holy status seems odd for an object used in the Temple service, so רבינא asks why it was not made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (this part is fine, but...)
Aim for it on purpose and take it

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם —
phrases.english: It makes sense that it held only two hands,
so that he should not aim for a lot and take it.
But why non-holy?
Let us make it holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one detail of רבא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that the קלפי was של חול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An object used in the Temple service should be made holy. Nothing seems to stop that.

steps.title: A holy vessel cannot be made of wood
steps.stepSummary: If the box were made holy, it would be a wooden כלי שרת. We do not make כלי שרת out of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it would be a holy vessel made of wood. We do not make holy vessels out of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא. The box could not be made holy because it was wooden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of רבא's details are connected. Because the box was wooden, it could not become a כלי שרת. So 'non-holy' is a result of 'wood'.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy vessel used in the Temple service

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן הָוֵה לֵהּ כְּלִי שָׁרֵת שֶׁל עֵץ,
phrases.english: If so, it would be a holy vessel of wood,
and we do not make a holy vessel of wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן הָוֵה לֵהּ כְּלִי שָׁרֵת שֶׁל עֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The box could simply be made holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wooden box cannot be a כלי שרת, so it stays חול.

steps.title: Why not make it of silver or gold?
steps.stepSummary: If wood is the problem, make the box out of silver or gold, and then it can be made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it be made of silver, or let it be made of gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. If the material is the only problem, change the material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer explained why a wooden box cannot be holy. It did not explain why the box had to be wooden. A metal box would fix the problem, so why use wood?

phrases.english: But let us make it of silver,
or let us make it of gold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer by offering a different material.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Precious metal could become a כלי שרת, so the box could have been holy.

steps.title: The Torah spares the people's money
steps.stepSummary: The box was not made of precious metal because the תורה does not want to waste the money of כלל ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה cares about the money of כלל ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. A cheap wooden box is used to avoid an unneeded expense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gold or silver box would cost a lot for no real need. Because of the principle of התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל, wood is used. Wood cannot be holy, so all three details of רבא now fit together.

keyTerms.term: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: The Torah cares about (spares) the money of the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: The קלפי was wooden to save money. Because it was wooden, it could not be a כלי שרת. It was small so the כהן גדול could not choose a lot on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle התורה חסה על ממונן של ישראל shows up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the silver/gold challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Use precious metal so the box can be holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: We avoid the expense, so the box is wooden and therefore חול.

steps.title: A ברייתא where the סגן also draws a lot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר. In his view, the סגן and the כהן גדול each put a hand in the box.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: The סגן and the כהן גדול put their hands into the box. If the lot for ה׳ comes up in the כהן גדול's right hand, the סגן says to him, 'My master כהן גדול, raise your right hand.' If it comes up in the סגן's right hand, the ראש בית אב says to the כהן גדול, 'Say your words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes the drawing differently from our משנה. In our משנה, the כהן גדול draws both lots himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, two people draw at once, each with his right hand. If the כהן גדול draws the lot for ה׳, the סגן tells him to raise his hand. If the סגן draws it, the ראש בית אב tells the כהן גדול to make the announcement.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow this תנא
Head of the priestly family on duty that day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In our משנה, the כהן גדול draws with both of his own hands. In this ברייתא, each person uses only his right hand.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in line with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: הַסְּגָן וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל מַכְנִיסִין יָדָן בַּקַּלְפִּי,
phrases.english: The deputy and the High Priest put their hands into the box.

phrases.aramaic: אִם בִּימִינוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה —
phrases.english: If the lot for ה׳ comes up in the High Priest's right hand,
the deputy says to him:
"My master, High Priest, raise your right hand."
And if it comes up in the deputy's right hand,

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב אוֹמֵר לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל:
phrases.english: the head of the priestly family says to the High Priest:
"Say your words."
phrases.notes: That is, declare the goat 'לה׳ חטאת'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the box itself to a different opinion about who draws the lots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the סגן and the כהן גדול each draw with the right hand.

steps.title: Why not have the סגן speak?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ראש בית אב speaks to the כהן גדול instead of the סגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the סגן say it to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a detail in the ברייתא. The סגן is already standing there and spoke in the first case, so why not let him speak here too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the סגן does the talking. In the second case, a different person suddenly speaks. The גמרא wants to know why the speaker changes.

phrases.english: But let the deputy say it to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a detail in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ראש בית אב, and not the סגן, tells the כהן גדול to speak

steps.title: To spare the כהן גדול's feelings
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול did not draw the lot for ה׳, so he may feel bad. If the סגן who drew it told him to speak, it could feel like teasing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the lot did not come up in his hand, he feels bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a different person speaks so the כהן גדול is not embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סגן 'won' the lot for ה׳, so the כהן גדול may already be upset. Hearing the order from the very person who won it would hurt more. So a neutral person, the ראש בית אב, says it instead.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבי אליעזר's view, the speaker changes to protect the כהן גדול's feelings. Our משנה does not follow this view: there, the כהן גדול draws both lots.

phrases.english: Since the lot did not come up in his hand,
he feels bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about who speaks.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סגן does not speak, so the כהן גדול is not hurt or embarrassed.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the argument between our משנה and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what basic idea causes our משנה and רבי יהודה to disagree about whether the סגן puts a hand into the box. This question sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 we learned that רבי יהודה has both the סגן and the כהן גדול draw lots, while our משנה has only the כהן גדול. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind each view, not just the two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root of an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument from step 15 and asks for its underlying reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates the משנה from רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Is the סגן's right hand better than the כהן גדול's left?
steps.stepSummary: One view says the סגן's right hand is better than the כהן גדול's left. The other says the two are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the right hand of the סגן is better than the left hand of the כהן גדול. The other master holds that they are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument depends on one question: what matters more, the right side or the more important person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the סגן's right hand is better than the כהן גדול's left. So he has the סגן draw with his right hand alongside the כהן גדול's right hand. That way the lot for ה׳ always comes up in a right hand. Our משנה holds the two are equal, so there is no reason to bring in the סגן. The כהן גדול alone draws with both hands.

keyTerms.meaning: they are equal to each other

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה says the right side means nothing. It only says that the סגן's right hand is not better than the כהן גדול's left hand.

phrases.english: One master holds: the right hand of the Segan
is better than the left hand of the High Priest.
And the other master holds: they are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: יַמִּינָא דִּסְגָן עֲדִיף מִשְּׂמָאלֵיהּ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether the סגן's right hand is better than the כהן גדול's left hand, or whether the two are equal.

steps.title: Who is the תנא who argues with רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the opposing view to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is this תנא who argues with רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the name of the תנא behind the view that the סגן does not take part in the lottery. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is written without a name. The גמרא wants to know which specific תנא holds that opposing view.

keyTerms.meaning: a Sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: And who is this tanna
who argues with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן הַאי תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the reasoning is clear, the גמרא asks who holds the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who argues with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: It is רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
steps.stepSummary: The opposing תנא is רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא who argues with רבי יהודה: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for this answer comes in the next step, from a ברייתא. רבי חנינא served as a סגן himself, so he knew firsthand what the סגן did.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי חנינא, the Deputy of the Kohanim

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Chanina, the Deputy of the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The opposing תנא is רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.

steps.title: The סגן stands ready only as a backup
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the סגן stands at the כהן גדול's right only so he can replace him if the כהן גדול becomes disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says: Why is the סגן at his right? So that if the כהן גדול becomes disqualified, the סגן can go in and serve in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי חנינא is the one who argues with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא gives only one reason for the סגן to be there: to replace the כהן גדול if he becomes disqualified. This shows that while the כהן גדול is fit, the סגן has no active job, so he would not draw the lots. That is the opposite of רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the role of the סגן on יום כיפור. He is a standby replacement, not a second partner in the service.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Chanina, the Deputy of the priests, says:
Why is the Deputy at his right?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵירַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: So that if a disqualification happens to the High Priest,
the Deputy can go in and serve in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the identification made in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חנינא is the תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the סגן's only purpose is to replace a disqualified כהן גדול.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים. The סגן is only a backup, so the כהן גדול draws both lots himself.

steps.title: In the days of שמעון הצדיק, the lot always came up on the right
steps.stepSummary: During the forty years that שמעון הצדיק served, the lot for ה׳ always came up in his right hand. After him, it varied.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: During the forty years that שמעון הצדיק served, the lot always came up in the right hand. From then on, sometimes it came up in the right and sometimes in the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא that lists signs of ה׳'s favor while שמעון הצדיק was כהן גדול. The first sign is that the lot for ה׳ always came up in his right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lot is normally random, so it coming up on the right side every year for forty years was a clear sign of Heavenly favor. After שמעון הצדיק, the lot became random again. This connects to our topic of the right hand in the lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: Shimon the Righteous, a famous כהן גדול

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The forty years that Shimon HaTzaddik served,
the lot would come up in the right hand.
From then onward,

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים עוֹלֶה בְּיָמִין פְּעָמִים עוֹלֶה בִּשְׂמֹאל.
phrases.english: sometimes it came up in the right, sometimes it came up in the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא, linked to the earlier discussion of the lot and the right hand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under שמעון הצדיק, the lot for ה׳ always came up on the right. After him, it varied.

steps.title: The red strip always turned white
steps.stepSummary: In שמעון הצדיק's time, the red strip of wool always turned white. After him, it only sometimes did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the strip of red wool would turn white. From then on, sometimes it turned white and sometimes it did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second sign: the red strip of wool always turned white, which showed that the people's sins were forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strip turning white was a sign of forgiveness, as the פסוק says that sins like red will become white as snow. Under שמעון הצדיק this happened every year. After him, it only happened sometimes.

phrases.english: And the strip of crimson wool would turn white.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ, פְּעָמִים מַלְבִּין פְּעָמִים אֵינוֹ מַלְבִּין.
phrases.english: From then onward, sometimes it turned white, sometimes it did not turn white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second sign to the list of signs in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The red strip always turned white under שמעון הצדיק, but not consistently after him.

steps.title: The western lamp kept burning
steps.stepSummary: In שמעון הצדיק's time, the western lamp of the מנורה kept burning. After him, it sometimes went out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the western lamp would stay lit. From then on, sometimes it stayed lit and sometimes it went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third sign: the western lamp of the מנורה kept burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The western lamp staying lit was a sign that the שכינה rested on the Jewish people. After שמעון הצדיק, this sign became inconsistent too.

keyTerms.meaning: the western lamp of the מנורה

phrases.english: And the western lamp would stay lit.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ, פְּעָמִים דּוֹלֵק פְּעָמִים כָּבֶה.
phrases.english: From then onward, sometimes it stayed lit, sometimes it went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third sign to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The western lamp burned steadily under שמעון הצדיק, but not consistently after him.

steps.title: The altar fire stayed strong
steps.stepSummary: In שמעון הצדיק's time, the fire on the מזבח stayed strong on its own, and the כהנים only added two logs to fulfill the מצוה. After him, they had to add wood all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the fire on the altar's woodpile stayed strong. The כהנים did not need to bring wood, except for two logs to fulfill the מצוה of bringing wood. From then on, sometimes it stayed strong and sometimes it did not, so the כהנים could not stop bringing wood all day long.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a fourth sign: the altar fire burned strongly by itself. After שמעון הצדיק, the כהנים had to keep feeding it all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמעון הצדיק, the כהנים added only two logs, and only because the Torah commands bringing wood. The fire itself did not need them. Later, the fire was not reliably strong, so the כהנים had to keep adding wood the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of placing wood on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The two logs were not needed to keep the fire going. They were added only to fulfill the מצוה, even when the fire did not need them.

phrases.english: And the fire of the altar's woodpile would stay strong,
and the priests did not need
to bring wood to the woodpile,
except for two logs of wood
in order to fulfill the מצוה of wood.
From then onward,
sometimes it stayed strong, sometimes it did not stay strong,
and the priests could not hold back
from bringing wood to the woodpile
the entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth sign to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The altar fire was strong by itself under שמעון הצדיק. After him, the כהנים had to feed it all day.
steps.whatToRemember: During the forty years of שמעון הצדיק, four signs of Heavenly favor were constant: the lot on the right, the red strip turning white, the western lamp burning, and the strong altar fire. After him, all four became inconsistent.

steps.title: A tiny portion of the holy breads filled each כהן
steps.stepSummary: In שמעון הצדיק's time, blessing rested on the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים. An olive-sized portion satisfied a כהן, and some even had leftovers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a blessing was sent into the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים. Every כהן who got an olive-sized piece: some ate it and were full, and some ate it and had some left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another miracle from שמעון הצדיק's time. The holy breads the כהנים ate had a special blessing in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps described miracles in the lots, the red wool, the מנורה, and the מזבח fire. This miracle is about food: a כזית is normally a tiny amount, yet it filled the כהן up. Some כהנים could not even finish it.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח; part of it was eaten by כהנים
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת and later eaten by the כהנים
Blessing; here, a miraculous abundance in the food
The size of an olive, a small halachic measure

phrases.english: And a blessing was sent into the omer,
and into the two loaves, and into the showbread.
And every priest whose share reached an olive's size,
some would eat it and be satisfied,
and some would eat it and leave some over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of miracles from שמעון הצדיק's time, now about the holy breads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שמעון הצדיק's time, an olive-sized portion of the holy breads miraculously satisfied each כהן.

steps.title: After שמעון הצדיק the blessing turned to a curse
steps.stepSummary: After שמעון הצדיק died, a curse entered the holy breads. Each כהן got only a bean-sized piece. Modest כהנים held back, while greedy ones grabbed and ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, a curse was sent into the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים, and each כהן got only a bean-sized piece. The modest כהנים pulled their hands back, and the greedy ones took and ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows the contrast: after שמעון הצדיק, the blessing on the breads was gone. The portions became so small that the modest כהנים did not bother taking their share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier steps: a miracle in his time, then decline after him. Here the decline is even stronger, since a curse replaced the blessing. The tiny portion also showed people's character: modest כהנים stepped back, and greedy ones grabbed.

keyTerms.meaning: From then on (after שמעון הצדיק's time)
The size of a bean (פּוֹל), even smaller than a כזית

steps.confusionAlert: כְּפוּל here does NOT mean "double." It means "like a bean" (כְּ + פּוֹל). The portion became smaller, not bigger.

phrases.english: From then on,
a curse was sent into the omer
and into the two loaves and into the showbread,
and each priest's share reached only a bean's size.
The modest ones would withdraw their hands,
and the gluttons would take and eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrast to step 27: what happened to the breads after שמעון הצדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שמעון הצדיק, a curse entered the holy breads; each כהן received only a bean-sized portion, and the modest held back while the greedy grabbed.

steps.title: The story of the כהן who took his friend's share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts a story about a greedy כהן who took both his own portion and his friend's, and people gave him a nickname.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about one כהן who took his own portion and his friend's portion, and people called him "בן..."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a real example of the greedy כהנים it just described. The nickname is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said the greedy ones took and ate. This story shows how far that went: one כהן took a share that belonged to someone else. The nickname was a public sign of shame for his behavior.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with one priest
who took his portion and his fellow's portion,
and they would call him "son of
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the nickname itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁנָּטַל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the greedy כהנים mentioned in step 28 with a specific story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A greedy כהן took his own and his friend's portion and was given a shaming nickname (completed on the next amud).
